headline: The Elementary School Building Committee narrowed Neary School renovation options, while the Select Board finalized positions on Special Town Meeting warrant articles.
synopsis: The Elementary School Building Committee voted to eliminate the most expensive design proposal for Neary Elementary School, narrowing focus to two architectural options and a $15 million baseline study ahead of Special Town Meeting. The Select Board reopened its October 17 warrant to endorse revised articles on two-family zoning and Community Preservation Act irrigation, while voting against CPA trail funding. Both the Affordable Housing Trust and the Municipal Technology Committee coordinated questions for the upcoming town satisfaction survey launching in October. The trust also examined options to invest roughly $1 million in idle funds, while town IT staff advanced municipal phone and firewall upgrades.

highlights.title: Neary School options narrowed to three paths
highlights.why: The committee voted to eliminate Option 4 and direct designers to focus on Options 1, 3, and a $15 million baseline after project cost projections ranged up to $49.2 million.

highlights.title: Select Board acts on Special Town Meeting warrant articles
highlights.why: The board voted to support revised articles on two-family zoning and CPA irrigation funding, but voted 1-4 against supporting CPA trails funding for the October 17 warrant.

highlights.title: Affordable Housing Trust explores investing cash reserves
highlights.why: Trustees initiated consultations with town finance staff to explore moving approximately $1 million currently held in near-zero interest accounts into higher-yield investments.

highlights.title: Satisfaction survey finalized for October launch
highlights.why: The committee prepared to launch the 2026 town satisfaction survey from October 1 through November 30, streamlining questions and incorporating input on affordable housing.

highlights.title: Neary traffic circulation and site layout refined
highlights.why: Architects proposed looping parent drop-offs around the rear cafeteria entrance while keeping buses at the front canopy to resolve queuing backups on the access road.

looking_ahead.what: Discussion on financial procurement policy and Breakneck Hill debt authorization
